items.title: Better welfare support needed for rural healthcare workers in Sabah
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Better welfare support is needed to encourage doctors and healthcare workers to remain in rural and remote areas of Sabah, said Sabah Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) chairman Dr Brandon Patrick Senagang. He said while the government's efforts to repair and upgrade health clinics, district hospitals and other healthcare facilities were welcomed, the welfare of the doctors and healthcare workers serving in them should not be overlooked. His call followed a town hall session with doctors in Keningau, including those serving in several rural and remote areas.

items.title: Malaysia targets first ‘made by Malaysia’ chips using Arm Limited technology by 2030, says economy minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — The government is targeting 2030 for the first “Made by Malaysia” chips developed using Arm Limited technology to enter production and the semiconductor supply chain. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said four companies have so far begun designing chips using technology from British semiconductor technology company Arm Limited, with the aim of eventually bringing their products into production and the semiconductor supply chain. Akmal said eight Arm technology-access packages — comprising four Arm CSS and four Arm Flexible Access tokens — had so far been offered to five local companies.

items.title: Tiktoker under police probe after allegedly stepping on Sarawak flag
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 21 — A TikToker is being investigated after uploading a video showing a man allegedly disrespecting Sarawak by deliberately stepping on the Ibu Pertiwi flag. Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the district police headquarters has received two reports regarding the incident. The TikToker allegedly uploaded similar content previously before deleting it several hours later.

items.title: Anwar: Wrongdoing at Tabung Haji, Felda must face action regardless of race
items.summary: BANGI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said allegations of wrongdoing involving Tabung Haji and Felda must be dealt with firmly, stressing that action should be taken regardless of whether those involved are Malay- or Muslim-linked. Anwar said governance and management weaknesses should not be turned into racial or religious issues, adding that Muslims should instead be held to a higher standard of ethics, integrity and accountability. In fact, if you ask me, Muslims must be even more serious and meticulous when it comes to ethics, management and values," he said at a session with Felda leadership and management here today.

items.title: Jardine Cycle & Carriage is selling its Malaysian, Singaporean business to Indonesia's Chandra Asri
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Jardine Cycle & Carriage Ltd (JC&C) is selling its Cycle & Carriage automotive businesses in Malaysia and Singapore to Indonesia's Chandra Asri Group for S$265 million (about US$207 million). "Overall, the proposed transaction enables JC&C to crystallise value from the Cycle & Carriage business as we focus on our core markets of Indonesia and Vietnam and deliver a positive outcome for shareholders, while positioning Cycle & Carriage for continued success under its new owner," it said in the bourse filing. JC&C said Cycle & Carriage would be well-positioned within the Chandra Asri Group ecosystem to leverage synergies and collaboration opportunities, strengthening its competitiveness and supporting future growth.

items.title: Bersatu must repair PN ties ahead of GE16, says Perlis MB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu must mend ties with its Perikatan Nasional (PN) partners and review its strategy ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16), said Perlis Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah. Bersatu must be part of a coalition," he said. On Perlis, he said Bersatu remained part of PN unless the party's central leadership decided otherwise.

items.title: Pahang retiree loses RM81,465 to online 'lover' he never met
items.summary: The man, in his 60s, had deposited the money after the woman claimed she needed financial assistance for various personal expenses, including buying jewellery and repairing her car. "The woman sought financial assistance, giving various excuses, including needing money to pay her room rental, repair her car, purchase jewellery and for personal use. The woman promised to meet the victim on Aug 10," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji CEO remanded seven days in MACC probe linked to RCI findings
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — A former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chief executive officer has reportedly been remanded for seven days to assist an investigation stemming from the findings of the royal commission of inquiry (RCI) into the pilgrims’ fund. Berita Harian reported that Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah issued the remand order, which runs until August 27, after allowing an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) at the Putrajaya Magistrates’ Court this morning. Separately, Malay Mail reported on August 15 that MACC had detained seven people in investigations arising from the RCI report, comprising a shipping company CEO, two company directors and four former members of TH’s senior management.

items.title: TM's data centre bet pays off as Nxera hits 70pct take-up
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Telekom Malaysia Bhd's (TM) data centre business is gaining traction, with about 70 per cent of the capacity at its TM Nxera data centre joint venture already contracted ahead of the first phase coming online next month. "TM's newly expanded Iskandar Puteri data centre capacity is fully taken up, with customers progressively moving in towards year-end," he said. TM's core profit after tax and minority interest rose 4.6 per cent year-on-year to RM406 million in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, while core earnings for the first half grew eight per cent to RM843 million.

items.title: Former TH CEO remanded 7 days over RCI report
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A former chief executive officer of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has been remanded for seven days in connection with the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into TH. BH reported yesterday that he was believed to be among the latest individuals being investigated by MACC in connection with the RCI report on TH. They included a former chief executive officer of a shipping company, a director of a construction company, a former company director and four former senior TH management personnel.

items.title: Anwar condemns Israeli tender for E1 settlement project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has condemned Israel's decision to issue construction tenders for the E1 settlement project east of Jerusalem, saying the move would undermine the prospect of a contiguous Palestinian state. Anwar said the tract of land had long been critical to the viability of a Palestinian state, adding that construction there would divide the West Bank. Building on it would divide the West Bank and gravely undermine the prospect of a contiguous Palestinian homeland," he said in a statement.

items.title: Putrajaya gears up for National Day bash, expects 80,000 visitors
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — More than 80,000 visitors are expected to flood Dataran Putrajaya in conjunction with National Day 2026, with preparations now reaching between 85 and 90 per cent. Ministry of Communications secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah said preparations involving various levels, including static training of all contingents, had begun in preparation for the celebration themed “Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati”. Also present were PPj president Datuk Mohd Sakeri Abdul Kadir and chief ceremonial officer of the Government Ceremony and Secretariat Division of the International Conference Datuk Rozainor Ramli.

items.title: Lee Lam Thye calls for tougher penalties for red-light runners
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Veteran social activist and Road Safety Council member Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye has called on the government to consider amending relevant road traffic laws to impose more severe penalties on red-light runners. He said stiffer penalties would send a clear message that traffic signals must be respected in the interest of everyone's safety. "Speeding and beating the traffic light is the most serious offence.

items.title: Immigration busts love scam, counterfeit goods syndicate, 21 held
items.summary: "Initial investigations found that the syndicate facilitated the entry of foreigners into Malaysia, including Chinese citizens believed to have been blacklisted by the Immigration Department. Zakaria said the operation team also seized four Chinese passports, four mobile phones and a Proton X70 believed to have been used by the syndicate. "The four alleged masterminds comprised two Chinese men, a Chinese woman and a Russian woman.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI probe: Former CEO arrives in Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court for remand
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — A former chief executive officer of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has arrived at the Magistrate’s Court here for remand proceedings related to investigations into a case linked to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on TH. The man, in his 60s, arrived at 9.35 am wearing an orange Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) remand shirt. The RCI report, which investigated issues concerning TH’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020, also listed problematic investments that require a forensic audit.

items.title: Parkson back on investors' radar, shares jump nearly 19pct ahead of Q2 results
items.summary: The stock opened flat at 18.5 sen before rising as much as 3.5 sen, or 18.92 per cent, to 22 sen, nearing its year-high of 22.5 sen recorded on Jan 5. At 11.17am, Parkson was trading at a six-month high of 21.5 sen, up three sen or 16.22 per cent, with 22.64 million shares changing hands. At 21.5 sen, the retail group and department-store operator had a market capitalisation of RM247.01 million.

items.title: Australia investigates fourth close call at Sydney airport in less than a month
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australia's transport safety regulator said on Friday it had launched an investigation into a fourth incident involving air traffic control at Sydney airport in less than a month after two planes were directed towards the same intersection on the ground. A Qantas Airbus A321 preparing to depart to the Gold Coast braked to avoid another Qantas aircraft, a Boeing 737, that had arrived from Melbourne on Tuesday, the Australian Transport Safety Bureau said in a statement. The Boeing had been cleared to continue along a taxiway that the Airbus had been cleared to turn onto, it said.

items.title: Charter plane carrying 8 crashes near remote site in western Alaska
items.summary: BENGALURU: A charter plane carrying eight people crashed near a remote radar site in western Alaska, the Associated Press said on Thursday, citing the National Transportation Safety Board. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: NexG, NexG Bina shares surge on government buyout prospect
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Shares of NexG Bhd and its associate NexG Bina Bhd surged in active trade after NexG confirmed that the government had sought an indicative price for a possible acquisition of its wholly owned subsidiary Datasonic Technologies Sdn Bhd (DTSB). NexG Bina, formerly known as Classita Holdings Bhd, was the third most actively traded counter, rising half a sen, or 16.67 per cent, to 3.5 sen, valuing it at about RM43 million. NexG Bina became an associate of NexG after the latter acquired a 32.61 per cent stake in the company in August 2025.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM AUGUST 21, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Friday, tracking Wall Street's weak close as geopolitical concerns weighed on investor sentiment. VS Industry, GIIB Holdings and BCM Alliance were among the most actively traded counters at the opening bell. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: 2 cyclists killed in Putrajaya road crash
items.summary: Putrajaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed said preliminary investigations found that the car, driven by a man in his 40s, had changed lanes from the middle lane to the left lane before hitting both victims at about 10.15pm. Aidi Sham said both victims suffered serious injuries to their faces and heads. "Members of the public or witnesses with information are urged to come forward to assist investigations by contacting the Putrajaya Traffic Police Station at 03-8886 2138 or any nearby police station," he said.

items.title: Missing angler found drowned after three-day search in Sungai Pahang
items.summary: TEMERLOH: An angler who was reported missing after falling into Sungai Pahang at Kampung Lebak Seberang while fishing on Aug 19 was found drowned today. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department public relations officer Zulfadli Zakaria said the search and rescue operation, which entered its third day today, involved six firefighters scouring the area where the victim was last seen. Firefighters from the Bukit Angin Fire and Rescue Station, along with divers from the department's underwater rescue team, were deployed to the river to assist in the search operation.

items.title: GOF raids seven illegal sand mining sites across three states, seizes RM13m worth of assets
items.summary: GOF Central Brigade commander SAC Hakemal Hawari said the operation to crack down on the activities began at 11am yesterday, covering the areas of Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Johor. Meanwhile, Hakemal said the latest raid at 3.30pm yesterday targeted an illegal operation site covering an area of 0.647 hectares at Lot PT 89, Jalan Lapangan Terbang Subang Lama, which is believed to be processing sand without permission. “The operation team also seized 1,500 tonnes of sand, heavy machinery and sand washing and processing equipment with an estimated value of RM5 million at this location alone,” he said after visiting the illegal site after the raid here last night.

items.title: Man held after threatening police with parang during raid
items.summary: JELI: A man was arrested after he allegedly threatened to kill police personnel with a parang during a raid at a house in Kampung Lubok Bongor here yesterday. Jeli district police chief Superintendent Kamarulzaman Harun said a team from the district Criminal Investigation Division conducted the raid at 11am following public tip-offs. "The suspect was later arrested," he said.

items.title: Asia shares downbeat on the week as bond yields, oil stay high
items.summary: Investors showed their scepticism by nudging 30-year bond yields back up to 5.25 per cent, while the 10-year hit 4.71 per cent. The strain was evident in the Nikkei which slipped 0.8 per cent, bringing losses for the week so far to 4.4 per cent. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan added 0.5 per cent.

items.title: Sarawak closes 591 schools as haze worsens
items.summary: KUCHING: A total of 591 schools in Sarawak were closed today as air quality deteriorated amid transboundary haze, with the API in Serian reaching 242. Eight other areas in Sarawak also recorded API readings, namely Sri Aman (189), Kuching (188), Samarahan (180), Sarikei (172), Sibu (156), Bintulu (153), Samalaju (36) and Kapit (107). Following deteriorating air quality due to transboundary haze, 591 schools under the supervision of 10 District Education Offices in Sarawak were closed today.

items.title: Oil set for second weekly rise as unsettled US-Iran war crimps supply
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Oil prices were little changed on Friday, but were on track for a second weekly rise as the stalemated US-Iran war continues to disrupt supply from the key Middle East producing region. Brent crude futures rose 4 cents to US$93.82 a barrel by 0142 GMT, after climbing 2.4 per cent in the previous session. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 6 cents to US$86.78 a barrel, after climbing 2.3 per cent in the prior session.

items.title: Dengue cases surge 56pc as MOH warns of nationwide spread
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has sounded the alarm over a significant surge in dengue cases across Malaysia, with infections spiking by more than 50 per cent compared to last year. Health officials attribute this rise to Malaysia's current volatile weather patterns. The ministry stressed that dengue control is a collective responsibility, particularly as more than 70 per cent of Aedes breeding sites are still located within residential premises.

items.title: Dollar wobbles as investors balk at US Treasury's rescue efforts
items.summary: Against a weaker dollar, the euro was perched near a three-month high and last bought US$1.1685, on track for a weekly rise of 1 per cent. Sterling flirted with a six-month peak and edged 0.08 per cent higher to US$1.3643, taking its gains for the week thus far to 0.8 per cent. In other currencies, the Australian dollar advanced 0.13 per cent to US$0.7123, while the New Zealand dollar added 0.23 per cent to US$0.5957 and was headed for a weekly rise of more than 1 per cent.

items.title: Gold steadies, heads for third straight weekly gain
items.summary: NEW YORK: Gold held steady on Friday but was on track for a third straight weekly gain, buoyed by a weaker dollar and US Treasury Department efforts to hold down longer-term yields. US gold futures steadied at US$4,571.20. Platinum rose 01.1 per cent to US$1,846.29, while palladium steadied at US$1,333.11.

items.title: [UPDATED] Hong Kong Tiananmen activists found guilty of inciting subversion
items.summary: HONG KONG: A Hong Kong court found on Friday two activists who organised annual vigils marking China's deadly Tiananmen crackdown in 1989 guilty of "incitement to subversion". Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, "incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power", a press summary handed out to reporters said. Lee and Chow were charged with subversion crimes in 2021 and have been behind bars since, under a Beijing-imposed national security law.

items.title: Japan manufacturing expands as orders rise fastest since 2018, PMI shows
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan's manufacturing sector expanded in August as new orders rose at their fastest pace since January 2018, a business survey showed on Friday. The S&P Global Flash Japan Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in August from 54.5 in July, a preliminary estimate by S&P Global showed. Services activity also strengthened in August.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji CEO arrives at Putrajaya Court for remand hearing
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A former chief executive officer (CEO) of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) arrived at the Putrajaya Court here for the hearing of an application to remand him. The man, in his 60s, arrived at 9.38am wearing an orange lock-up uniform and handcuffed, escorted by Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officers. Berita Harian is seeking confirmation from the MACC chief commissioner on the matter.

items.title: Any lane, any time: Plus activates JustGo ANPR toll payments across North-South Expressway minus Penang Bridge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Plus Malaysia has activated its JustGo toll payment system across the entire North-South Expressway (NSE) network, except the Penang Bridge, using automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) to allow motorists to pay tolls through any available lane. Under the JustGo framework, a registered vehicle’s plate number anchors the payment process. To activate the service, motorists must download the JustGo app on Android or iOS and register their vehicle plate number.

items.title: Anwar impressed by Sukma’s young athletes, hopes to see them represent country
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim hopes the young athletes competing in the 2026 Selangor Malaysia Games (Sukma) will go on to represent Malaysia on the international stage. “Hopefully, they will one day have the opportunity to represent Malaysia and make the country proud on the international stage,” he said. Selangor is hosting the biennial games again after 28 years, with more than 5,000 young athletes from across the country competing for 468 gold medals in 37 sports until August 24.

items.title: 14 Pontian landowners served notices over Singapore construction waste dumping
items.summary: PONTIAN: Fourteen landowners whose properties were being used as dumping sites for construction waste from Singapore have been issued with notices by the Pontian Municipal Council (MPPn). Council president Sulaiman Ismail said 11 of the 14 locations had been closed off, with notices placed at the entrances to the sites, reported Kosmo!. He said most of the locations were in Mukim Sungai Karang, while several others were in Mukim Pontian, Mukim Jeram Batu/Pengkalan Raja and Mukim Serkat.

items.title: Two cyclists die in Putrajaya after vehicle hits them while changing lanes, say police
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — Two cyclists died after being hit by a vehicle at kilometre 9.0 of Jalan Persiaran Selatan, Putrajaya, last night, said Putrajaya district police chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed. In a statement today, Aidi Sham said the accident occurred at 10.15pm, involving a vehicle driven by a local man in his 40s and two male cyclists aged in their 40s and 30s respectively. “Initial investigations found that the vehicle being driven had changed direction from the middle lane to the left lane before hitting the two cyclists.

items.title: BTH: Fair EPF returns and govt's pre-budget statement [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economy may be growing, with unemployment low and inflation relatively contained. Yet many Malaysians continue to feel financially squeezed, struggling with rising living costs, mounting commitments and inadequate savings. The issue said Ida should also be viewed through the wider public interest, particularly as many Malaysians risk reaching retirement with inadequate savings.

items.title: Serian records very unhealthy air quality as of 9am
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Eight areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with Serian registering a very unhealthy reading, as of 9am today. Meanwhile, 56 areas nationwide recorded moderate readings ranging from 51 to 97, while three others registered good air quality, with readings below 50. API readings of 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, and 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings exceeding 300 are categorised as hazardous.

items.title: Police hunt suspects after attempted armed robbery of Klang gold shop leaves one injured
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 21 — Police are hunting for suspects believed to be involved in an attempted robbery of a gold shop at Jalan Tengku Kelana, Klang, near here, yesterday morning, which has gone viral on social media. Klang Selatan district deputy police chief Supt Kamalariffin Aman Shah confirmed the incident. “Klang Selatan district police headquarters (IPD) Criminal Investigation Division has opened an investigation paper under Section 394 of the Penal Code for causing hurt during an attempted gang robbery.

items.title: GOF 'buries' eight-year illegal sand operation, with RM5mil in seizures [WATCH]
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: An illegal sand processing operation, which sold sand for RM600 per truckload and moved between 30 and 60 loads daily, is believed to have been operating for about eight years. GOF Central Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Hakemal Hawari said the operation involved bringing unwanted sand from elsewhere, including construction sites, to the site for processing. "The processed fine sand was then sold for RM600 per truckload, with between 30 and 60 lorries transporting the sand out daily," he said when met last night.

items.title: Serian API hits ‘Very Unhealthy’ level of 241 as Sarawak air quality worsens
items.summary: The Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) in an update at 5.32pm on Thursday said dry conditions prevailed over most parts of the southern Asean region except over the northern parts of Borneo where some showers were observed. Scattered to widespread hotspots were detected in Indonesia’s Kalimantan and Sumatra, while few to isolated hotspots were detected elsewhere in the southern Asean region. “Moderate to dense smoke plumes were also observed to emanate from hotspot clusters detected in many parts of Kalimantan and the southern parts of Sumatra.

items.title: MCMC: Scammers turn to RCS, iMessage after hyperlink restrictions on SMS
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 21 — Online scams have been detected shifting to messaging services such as Rich Communication Services (RCS) and iMessage to spread phishing links following the enforcement of hyperlink restrictions on short messaging service (SMS). Selangor Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) Telecommunications Fraud deputy director Mohd Amirul Hakim Abdul Rahim said the shift was detected as these messaging services still allowed the transmission of hyperlinks to users for phishing purposes. Besides the MCMC representative, the forum featured National Financial Crime Centre (NFCC) director-general Datuk Seri Shamshun Baharin Mohd Jamil, Selangor Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) chief SAC Mohamad Rosni Mohamed Lazim and Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) LINK and Offices Department (JLPB) deputy director Hasjun Hashim as panellists.

items.title: Kuantan police corporal jailed nine months after Court of Appeal reinstates RM700 bribery conviction
items.summary: A three-judge panel, comprising Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz, and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, also upheld the Sessions Court’s order that Mohamed Syaffiq Mohamed Sidek, 36, pay a RM10,000 fine, or serve 12 months’ jail in default. The panel allowed the prosecution’s cross-appeal and dismissed Mohamed Syaffiq’s appeal against his conviction and sentence. Lawyers Datuk Sukri Mohamed, Melissa Sukri and Shahidah Muslimah Roslan represented Mohamed Syaffiq.

items.title: Sabah Immigration repatriates 4,750 undocumented migrants so far this year
items.summary: TAWAU, Aug 21 — The Sabah Immigration Department has repatriated 4,750 illegal immigrants of various nationalities to their respective countries so far this year. In a statement yesterday, the Sabah Immigration Department said Filipinos accounted for the highest number at 3,008, followed by Indonesians (1,478), Pakistanis (118), Chinese (109), Vietnamese (18) and 19 others of various nationalities. The Sabah Immigration Department urged the public to channel any information or complaints regarding illegal immigrant activities through the Public Complaints Management System (SISPAA) portal or the Online Enquiry System (SPO).

items.title: Fadhlina pushes swift investigation into alleged bullying, racial discrimination at KL school after student’s death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Schools Inspectorate, District Education Office and Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Education Department have been directed to promptly complete an internal investigation into the alleged bullying and discrimination at a school here recently. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said matters of public concern, including those related to bullying and racial elements, must be taken seriously and addressed promptly based on facts and due processes. At the same time, Fadhlina said attention and appropriate support were also being provided to the affected families, students, teachers and the entire school community.

items.title: Penang land scandal: MACC arrests government agency chairman, four others over undervalued sales
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has detained five individuals, including the chairman of a government agency, for allegedly exploiting their positions in the disposal of eight plots of land in Penang. The suspects, aged between their 40s and 50s, include a chairman with a Datuk title, two company directors, a technical manager, and a clerk, TV3 reported. Sources indicate that the chairman allegedly abused his dual roles as deputy chairman and board member in 2015 to sanction the sale of eight plots of land in Seberang Perai Selatan.

items.title: MOE studying co-curricular recognition for prison school students seeking university admission
items.summary: KAJANG, Aug 21 — The Education Ministry (MOE) will look into awarding merit for participation in co-curricular activities, including sports, by students at prison institutions for consideration in university admission. Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the move was important to ensure that these students have the opportunity to pursue higher education after completing the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) and leaving the institutions. Besides co-curricular merit, she said the ministry would also discuss with the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) division the possibility of awarding skills certificates to students who undergo skills training while at prison institutions.

items.title: CAAM orders Malaysian airlines to drug-test 100pc of active flight and cabin crew
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) has introduced enhanced regulatory measures to strengthen fitness-for-duty requirements and prevent alcohol and drug misuse among aviation personnel performing safety-critical functions. In a statement yesterday, CAAM said the measures were part of its continued commitment to safeguarding the safety, security and integrity of Malaysia’s civil aviation system. On 7 August 2026, CAAM issued Safety Directive 02/2026 — Strengthening Fitness-for-Duty and Prevention of Alcohol and Drug Misuse, introducing enhanced requirements for flight crew and cabin crew performing safety-critical functions.

items.title: Anwar visits Brunei for annual leaders’ consultation with Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah
items.summary: BANDAR SERI BEGAWAN, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will be on a working visit to Brunei today and tomorrow to attend the 27th Annual Leaders’ Consultation (ALC-27) between Malaysia and Brunei. Malaysian High Commissioner to Brunei Datuk Mohd Aini Atan said this annual leaders’ consultation series serves as the highest-level bilateral mechanism between Malaysia and Brunei. In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and Brunei was recorded at RM5.86 billion (US$1.37 billion).

items.title: ‘No leniency, no mercy’: Family demands justice over Immigration lorry crash that killed three on Jalan Sultan Ismail
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The family of three people killed when an Immigration Department lorry ploughed into them in Jalan Sultan Ismail has called for the driver to face the full force of the law, with no allowances made for his status as a civil servant. The sole survivor, Firdaus’ widow Norhayati Rozali, 55, remains hospitalised with serious injuries. Speaking for the grieving family, her brother Azlan Rozali, 48, urged the authorities to resolve the case swiftly and without favour, NST reported.

items.title: MACC to seek remand for former Tabung Haji chief exec over RCI findings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — A former chief executive officer of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) is set to face a remand application today to assist in investigations following the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the pilgrimage fund. The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is expected to file the application at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court at 9am, The Star reported. The RCI report, which was made public via the Malaysian Islamic Development Department (Jakim) portal on July 29, scrutinised several high-level issues regarding TH’s operations.

items.title: Haze: Staying indoors cuts exposure but won’t make your home pollution-free, experts say
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — As the haze returns to Malaysia, staying indoors is often the simplest way to reduce exposure to polluted air. Tan, whose work focuses on indoor air quality, said conventional residential air conditioning units are generally sufficient to help maintain indoor air quality because they recirculate indoor air rather than drawing air directly from outside. “Home air conditioners are in a way, ‘air purifiers’ themselves because they have filters inside and can filter haze particulate matter if any is present indoors (when they draw air from the room).

items.title: Kedah MB’s ex‑political secretary ordered to enter defence in REE mining bribery case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — The Sessions Court today ordered Mohamad Hilmi Abdul Wahab, former political secretary to the Kedah Menteri Besar, to enter his defence on two charges of soliciting and accepting bribes in connection with rare earth element (REE) mining projects three years ago. Judge Suzana Hussin made the ruling after finding that the prosecution had successfully established a prima facie case against Mohamad Hilmi, 53, at the close of its case. Accordingly, the accused is ordered to enter his defence,” said Suzana.

items.title: Former CEO unaware why 1MDB accused him of fraud in separate suit, court hears
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — Former Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) chief executive officer Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi told the High Court today that he did not know why allegations made against him by the company in a separate suit filed in August 2021 had changed. The 56-year-old was testifying as the fourth plaintiff witness in 1MDB’s US$5.64 billion civil suit filed in May 2021 against eight defendants, including former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak. During cross-examination, senior counsel G.K. Ganesan, representing former 1MDB investment director Kelvin Tan Kay Jin, referred Shahrol Azral to allegations made against him in a suit filed by 1MDB against Deutsche Bank and other parties in August 2021.

items.title: Anwar to attend 27th Annual Leaders’ Consultation during two‑day working visit to Brunei beginning tomorrow
items.summary: BANDAR SERI BEGAWAN, Aug 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will be on a working visit to Brunei on August 21 and 22 to attend the 27th Annual Leaders’ Consultation (ALC-27) between Malaysia and Brunei. Malaysian High Commissioner to Brunei Datuk Mohd Aini Atan said this annual leaders’ consultation series serves as the highest-level bilateral mechanism between Malaysia and Brunei. In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and Brunei was recorded at RM5.86 billion (US$1.37 billion).

items.title: Anwar: Major announcements coming on Aug 30, Sept 16 and during Budget tabling
items.summary: KLANG, Aug 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to make several important announcements, including one on the eve of National Day on August 30 and another during the Malaysia Day celebrations on September 16. The Prime Minister said the government was strengthening protection for gig economy workers through the establishment of the Malaysian Gig Economy Commission (SEGiM) and the introduction of a new bill concerning small businesses. Meanwhile, Anwar said the government would facilitate access to financing for graduates seeking to venture into business, including through the National Entrepreneurial Group Economic Fund (TEKUN).

items.title: Anwar orders probe into Khazanah subsidiary Xeraya Capital over potential financial irregularities
items.summary: KLANG, Aug 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered a comprehensive investigation into Xeraya Capital, a wholly owned subsidiary of Khazanah Nasional Bhd, to identify any potential financial irregularities. Anwar, who is also Khazanah chairman, said a meeting with the board this morning had uncovered concerns over the governance of a company established in 2012. During the Board meeting, Khazanah, in line with its governance standards, raised legacy issues that need to be resolved, including those involving Xeraya Capital, which manages Khazanah’s life sciences investments.

items.title: Umno to discuss whether to go solo or cooperate in Melaka polls at Aug 28 MT meeting
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 20 — Umno’s political direction, including whether to cooperate with other parties or go solo in the Melaka state election, will be discussed at the Umno Supreme Council (MT) meeting on August 28. Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan said the meeting, to be chaired by president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, would also discuss the best strategy to ensure Barisan Nasional’s (BN) victory in the state election. BN formed the state government after winning 21 of the 28 seats in the 15th Melaka state election, followed by PH with five seats and PN with two.

items.title: Nanta: Rebuild of SK Felda Kota Gelanggi 1’s dilapidated building finished 310 days ahead of schedule
items.summary: JERANTUT, Aug 20 — The reconstruction of a dilapidated building at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Felda Kota Gelanggi 1 here has been completed 310 days ahead of schedule, enabling pupils to enjoy more comfortable and conducive learning facilities. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the RM7.998 million project was completed ahead of schedule without any extension of time (EOT), demonstrating good performance in the implementation of government projects. “This means the project was completed nearly a year ahead of schedule, or more than 300 days ahead.
